content: Hi, how can I support your content project today?
I run a small gift shop and want to send a quick SMS to customers about our Spring Sale. Can you help me draft one?

Absolutely! For a promotional SMS, it's most effective to include: a friendly greeting, a mention of the Spring Sale, a highlight of special items or discounts, and a warm call-to-action. Keeping it concise ensures it's easy to read and inviting. Would you like it to sound cheerful or more formal?
Cheerful, please. Here's my first try: "Hey! Spring Sale at Blossom Gifts. 20% off select items. Stop by soon!"

That's a great start! To enhance it, I'd suggest adding a sense of freshness that ties into spring, and a gentle nudge to visit soon. For example, mentioning new arrivals or seasonal gifts can create interest. Also, including your shop name at the end helps with recognition.
Good idea. Can you show me how that would look?

Sure! Here's a revised version: "Hello from Blossom Gifts! Celebrate Spring with 20% off select seasonal items and discover our newest arrivals. Visit us soon and bring a little sunshine home! - Blossom Gifts"
I like the sunshine part. Should I make the call-to-action more urgent, or is that enough?

Your current call-to-action is friendly and inviting, which matches your cheerful tone. It encourages customers to visit without feeling pressured. If you want a slight boost, you could mention the sale is for a limited time, but even as-is, it feels welcoming and on brand.
Thanks! I'll use this version for my Spring Sale SMS.
